rationale: Economically coherent and sign-consistent, but (GP−dp−xint)/GP is just 1 minus the sum of the two already-archived burden ratios inside the identical cheap gate, so it is closer to a re-parameterization than a new mechanism — and the claim that it is "free of sign flips" is wrong, since firms with negative gross profit get a large positive (good) score from the same deductions.

Treating dividends as a prior "claim" that destroys equity value is economically incoherent (dividends accrue to the equity holder, and the archived dividend result was conditional on a high-yield gate, not a generic burden), and the four-term aggregate is explicitly assembled by sign-fitting to in-sample archive t-stats rather than from a prior.

Level-plus-flow of claims on gross profit is a defensible pairing with a correct diagnosis of why the gen-3 SUMRANK fusion failed, though it remains a recombination of two archived grading channels under the same gate and inherits their negative-gross-profit denominator instability.

This is essentially gross-profit-to-price (Novy-Marx's valuation-ratio version of gross profitability) with depreciation and interest netted out — a known published value ratio, not a cross-theme interaction, and it abandons the interaction mandate entirely to test a single univariate yield.

A genuine mechanism-location test that runs the validated burden channel in the opposite valuation state with an internally consistent expected sign and a construction directly comparable to the cheap-gate signals, so either outcome is informative about whether the effect is distress-specific.

Pairing the net-cash gate (strong FMB, weak alpha) with the capital-consumption channel (weak FMB, reliable alpha) is a sensible attempt to reconcile the two evidence types, but the grading leg is monotone-equivalent to an archived one, and the stated microcap fix is doubtful since dp/GP proxies asset intensity rather than cash burn and inverts for negative-gross-profit firms.
